description: Thailand proforma defaults for the Rofu (Keen) case. Entries whose source is the placeholder marker are benchmark estimates awaiting confirmation from Keen and must render with a visible marker on the Assumptions sheet.
cost_currency_note: Every per-kW, per-kWh and lump-sum cost in the "financial" block is USD, matching REopt's own installed_cost_per_kw convention. PEA tariff figures are THB and live in pea_tariff_rates.json. Convert with financial.exchange_rate_thb_per_usd.

project_years.source: Client direction 2026-09-09: 20-year project life. Supersedes the earlier 25-year convention carried over from the Vietnam cases.
project_years.note: Every scheduled event still falls inside the horizon: debt term 10 years, inverter replacement year 11; the battery is not replaced (2026-09-12), its fade is carried by the SOH curve. The inverter therefore serves 9 of the 20 years after replacement, against 14 of 25 before, so the concern about an ageing inverter fleet in the back half is reduced rather than worsened.

discount_rate.note: Value carried forward from Saelim, S. (Agora Energiewende, on behalf of CASE for Southeast Asia, implemented with TDRI), "Policy instruments for facilitating rooftop solar PV investments: Thailand and international cases," 16 Aug 2024: risk waterfall for Thai rooftop PV investment puts the cost of equity at 11.5 percent under business-as-usual (current) risk conditions. Cross-checked against Farungsang, Varquez and Tokimatsu, "Geospatial Assessment and Economic Analysis of Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic Potential in Thailand," MDPI Sustainability 17(15):7052 (Aug 2025), which used 6.3145 percent, described there as reflecting the 2022 Bank of Thailand policy rate. Accessed 2026-09-06. This 11.5 percent is a third-party developer's cost of equity, carrying explicit developer risk and permitting risk premiums that do not apply to Rofu, which is a factory self-investing in its own roof rather than a third-party developer. Rofu's actual cost of capital is unknown and is likely lower, so 11.5 percent is used here as a conservative figure pending Keen's confirmation of the real hurdle rate.

pv_installed_cost_per_kw.source: Client direction 2026-09-09: 500 USD/kWp, the top of the client-confirmed C&I rooftop range of 450 to 500 USD/kWp. Supersedes the 475.0 midpoint used in the prior run.
pv_installed_cost_per_kw.note: This remains below every published Thai benchmark this project located. Krungsri Research gives THB 20,000-25,000/kWp for C&I rooftop, which is USD 615-769 at 32.5 THB/USD, and Farungsang, Varquez and Tokimatsu, MDPI Sustainability 17(15):7052 (Aug 2025), assumes USD 767/kWp. Returns scale directly off this figure, so it must be disclosed as client-supplied rather than benchmarked.

bess_replacement_enabled.source: Client direction 2026-09-12: no scheduled battery replacement inside the 20 year horizon; capacity fade is carried by the Battery SOH curve and derates the battery's savings instead.
bess_replacement_enabled.note: Supersedes the year-10 whole-system replacement at 100 percent of install (2026-09-11). A case may still opt in through technologies.storage.replacement in its case.json; the policy year (10) and fraction (1.0) are then inherited. REopt is sent replace_cost_per_kw = replace_cost_per_kwh = 0

bess_cycle_life_efc.source: Client direction 2026-09-12: 8,000 equivalent full cycles to 80 percent state of health, LFP datasheet convention.
bess_cycle_life_efc.note: Sets the cycle-fade coefficient of the SOH curve: (1 - 0.80) / 8000 = 2.5e-5 kWh lost per kWh discharged. NREL's laboratory default (2.46e-5) corresponds to about 8,130 cycles, so the curve barely moves; the assumption is now a vendor-style input rather than a laboratory constant. Calendar fade keeps NREL's coefficients

annual_om_per_kw.source: Client direction: O&M set at 1.5 percent of PV capex. 500.0 * 0.015 = 7.5 USD/kWp/yr.
annual_om_per_kw.note: Farungsang, Varquez and Tokimatsu, "Geospatial Assessment and Economic Analysis of Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic Potential in Thailand," MDPI Sustainability 17(15):7052 (Aug 2025), the paper previously cited for pv_installed_cost_per_kw, assumes O&M at 1 percent of installed capex per year for its Thai rooftop PV economic analysis. That is a published lower bound, not the value used here: the client has directed 1.5 percent. Accessed 2026-09-06. Re-derive this figure if pv_installed_cost_per_kw ever changes, since it is 1.5 percent of that value rather than an independently sourced number.

debt_interest_rate.source: Thai commercial bank Minimum Loan Rates (MLR), Dec 2025: Siam Commercial Bank cut to 6.400 percent effective 23 Dec 2025, Bangkok Bank cut to 6.45 percent effective 22 Dec 2025, KBank cut to 6.62 percent effective 22 Dec 2025 (scb.co.th; Nation Thailand, nationthailand.com/business/banking-finance/40060060). Cross-checked against Saelim, S. (Agora Energiewende / CASE for Southeast Asia / TDRI), 16 Aug 2024, which gives a project-specific cost of debt for Thai rooftop PV of 5.3 percent under business-as-usual conditions. The bank MLR figures are more current and more directly a commercial lending rate; 6.5 percent is carried as the conservative (higher) end of that MLR band. Accessed 2026-09-06.
debt_interest_rate.note: Replaces the prior 0.06 placeholder. 6.5 percent rounds the 6.40-6.62 percent MLR band rather than averaging it exactly, staying on the conservative side.

grid_connection_cost.note: Excluded from capex at client direction (spec D10), the same direction covering power_factor_mitigation_cost. 10,000 THB PEA connection charge at 32.5 THB/USD. Cited range for PEA/MEA grid-connection fees is 5,000-15,000 THB, so this is immaterial at project scale. Physical protection, metering and any transformer work normally sit inside the EPC scope and belong in pv_installed_cost_per_kw. See docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-04-thai-depreciation.md

permitting_and_eia_cost.note: EIA and IEE are genuinely NOT required: the thresholds are 5 MWp for an IEE and 10 MWp for an EIA, and this project is about 1.7 MWp. Zero is therefore correct for the environmental component, not a stub. The Aor.6 building-modification permit and the ERC generation licence (triggered at 1 MWp) ARE required but have no public fee schedule, so they are excluded and must be disclosed as excluded. See docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-04-thai-depreciation.md

power_factor_mitigation_cost.note: Excluded from capex at client direction (spec D10): the site kVAR maximum was never requested, so this is a client choice, not a technical finding that no mitigation is needed.

pv_inverter_replacement_year.note: String inverters are normally replaced once inside a 20-year analysis. Year 11 matches the ENS SolarStorage calculation form supplied in the client folder. Shared replacement policy: both countries book this event

pv_inverter_replacement_fraction_of_pv_c.note: Inverter share of PV capex, from the ENS SolarStorage calculation form. Re-benchmarked for Thailand in Task 15. Shared replacement policy: both countries book this fraction

bess_min_duration_hours.note: REopt inherits 0.0, which permits a physically meaningless zero-duration battery. 1.5 hours is the shortest duration a C&I lithium system is normally offered at

bess_om_fraction_of_installed_cost.note: REopt's own default is 2.5 percent, a US figure. Re-benchmarked for Thailand in Task 15

cit_standard_rate.source: Thai Revenue Code standard corporate income tax rate

pv_depreciation_years.source: Thai Revenue Code, Royal Decree No. 145: plant, machinery and equipment depreciate at up to 20 percent per year, a 5-year straight line. See docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-04-thai-depreciation.md for the PV machinery-versus-building-improvement caveat

bess_depreciation_years.source: Thai Revenue Code, Royal Decree No. 145: plant, machinery and equipment depreciate at up to 20 percent per year, a 5-year straight line. See docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-04-thai-depreciation.md for the PV machinery-versus-building-improvement caveat

grid_emission_factor_kg_co2e_per_kwh.source: Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organization (TGO), official emission-factor table for Carbon Footprint for Organization (CFO) Scope 2 reporting (thaicarbonlabel.tgo.or.th, document dated UPDATE February 2026): electricity grid-mix (average) factor for 2022-2024 generation data is 0.4750 kgCO2e/kWh, effective 1 Jan 2026. This supersedes the 2016-2018 vintage grid-mix factor of 0.4999 kgCO2e/kWh, which is the value this placeholder previously carried and which the same TGO table states remains usable only through 31 Mar 2026. Cross-checked against Thailand's Energy Policy and Planning Office (EPPO) generation-only CO2 intensity of 0.399-0.400 kgCO2/kWh for 2023-2024 (a narrower-scope figure: CO2 only, excludes CH4, N2O and T&D losses, so a lower number than TGO's is expected and not a red flag). An attempt to cross-check against the IGES/IFI harmonised grid-factor list was blocked by the source site and could not be verified. Accessed 2026-09-06.
grid_emission_factor_kg_co2e_per_kwh.note: This is TGO's grid-mix (average) Scope 2 factor, not an operating-margin, build-margin or combined-margin figure. proforma_thailand/emissions.py computes avoided Scope 2 emissions, so the Scope 2 grid-mix factor is the methodologically correct choice; a T-VER/CDM-style combined-margin factor serves a different purpose (carbon-credit MRV) and should not be substituted here.

grid_emission_factor_vintage.value: 2022-2024 generation data (TGO CFO Scope 2 grid-mix average, effective 1 Jan 2026)
grid_emission_factor_vintage.source: Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organization (TGO) CFO emission-factor table, thaicarbonlabel.tgo.or.th, document dated UPDATE February 2026. Accessed 2026-09-06.

pv_tilt_degrees.note: Approximates both the site latitude of 15.21N and a typical industrial metal roof pitch. Actual roof pitch is not recorded in the RTS Data Collection sheet and is an information request to Ou
